what_matters.head: US stocks fell about 2% even as Anthropic's debut closed 17% above its IPO price
what_matters.detail: The S&P 500 was up as much as 1.3% in the morning, then closed down about 2%, 8.2% below its October high (AP). CNBC names the Nvidia scandal and worries that AI chip sales to Asia will slow as Washington tightens export-control enforcement. Anthropic opened about 34% above its $83 IPO price and closed 17% above it.

what_matters.head: Gold fell 5.1%, about 3.4 × its usual day, to its lowest in about 14 months
what_matters.detail: CNBC ties it to a firmer dollar and bets on a December Fed rate rise. The dollar index was flat on the day (−0.03%) and is up 2.0% in a month. The Fed's minutes, out on 18 Nov, said nearly all officials expect a quarter-point increase in December (AP).

what_matters.head: WeRide reports Q3 results today after falling 11% (3.0 × usual) on Thursday
what_matters.detail: No reported cause was found for Thursday's fall. Analyst estimates are in yuan, so no dollar bar is given. The check is revenue and gross margin against Q2's RMB 231.7M and 37.5%.

latest.tape_note: A broad US down day: more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell, the index's longest losing streak since 2024 (AP). 30 of the 34 names here fell in their latest session and 32 are below their 50-day average. The VIX, which rises when traders pay more to protect against big moves in US stocks, closed at 28.4. That is 70% higher than a month ago and its highest in these daily reports since 31 March. Chip stocks fell 2.8% on the day, 11% over five days and 19% in a month. Gold fell 5.1%, about 3.4 × usual.
latest.tonight: WeRide's Q3 results, with the call at 21:00 SGT. The University of Michigan's final November consumer sentiment reading is due at about 23:00 SGT.
